2.text: during the spring fair on the Wolverene River, I was present at a series of

3.text: reindeer-races in the camps of the richest inhabitants. Two persons were all

4.text: the time striving against each other for the victory. Their names were

5.text: Toˊlɪño and Yaˊtirg̣ɪn. The reindeer of Toˊlɪño, however, were better than those

6.text: of his rival, and he was victor several times. Then, at one race, the right

7.text: reindeer of his team suddenly stumbled and fell, not fifty feet distant from

8.text: the goal, which gave to Yaˊtirg̣ɪn the chance to snatch the prize first. Of

9.text: course, the accident was ascribed to a harmful incantation of the kind known

10.text: as eiˊᵋut.¹ In my presence the uncle of Toˊlɪño, frightened by the accident,

11.text: tried to persuade him to stop racing and prepare for the return journey to his

12.text: camp, which was two hundred miles distant. Toˊlɪño was obstinate, and

13.text: determined to continue. Two days later, to the horror of all, Toˊlɪño died

14.text: suddenly. The death, of course, was ascribed to the witchery of his rival;

15.text: the more so, as the latter with his family left the country hastily on the next

16.text: day, and went eastward in the direction of the Chaun River. In his haste,

17.text: he even left behind a part of his large herd of reindeer, which were taken by the

18.text: family of the deceased. The brother of the latter promised to visit, the next

19.text: fall, the country of Chaun in order to settle the blood-score.

20.text: In another case, which happened the same year at the Anui fair, one

21.text: Chukchee accused his neighbor of killing his son by witchcraft a few months

22.text: before that time. The two families were not very friendly, and it seems that

23.text: the supposed wizard, when under the influence of brandy, was wont to boast

24.text: of his magic skill. Be that as it may, the father, thirsting for revenge,

25.text: watched for the wizard as he was passing on a trail among the camps, and

26.text: shot him down with a rifle. The brothers of the murdered man wanted to

27.text: have blood for blood; but even they felt that the wronged father was within

28.text: his right, and after some controversy the affair was settled without even weregild.

29.text: DIVINATION. — Of the methods of divination, the most common is that

30.text: with a suspended object. The Chukchee and the Eskimo alike use for this

32.text: pebble with a string tied around it may serve the purpose, although stones

33.text: somewhat bizarre in form are preferred. Often the skull of an animal (Fig.

34.text: 297, a) is used for the purpose, a “wooden spirit”² (Fig. 297, b), a rough image

35.text: of a “guardian,” or even a piece of wood cut off under peculiar circumstances.
